frames: Engine axes, metres: X right, Y forward, Z up. Plate rectangles are in the plate mesh frame (the holo layer reads correctly from -Y). inSlot is the plate component in the frame of the entity slot its binding chain ends on (vehicle_slots for most cars). yaw ~0 = rear plate, ~180 = front.

quadPlacement.note: Cover rule (native/cover.cjs). The quad lies proudMetres in front of the holo layer's outermost point; a visible plate surface within clearanceMetres of that plane and within parallelDegrees of parallel to it pushes the quad out in front of it. The quad covers the holo rectangle grown on every side by gap * tan(coverMaxViewDegrees) + coverExtraMetres, gap being the distance from the quad to the deepest holo point, so no ray leaving the holo within coverMaxViewDegrees of the plate normal can miss it. The build casts those rays (leak*: one sample per leakStepMetres squared, leakAzimuths azimuths per cone angle) and fails on any print seen. mountHidesHolo: a mounted plate, which is ours, is authored with its holo chunk masked out of chunkMask, as vanilla hides whole plates on burnt definitions (chunkMask 0). legacyMarginMetres: the superseded fit rule (quad inside the holo at legacyAspect, proudMetres in front of every vertex over the holo grown by this margin), measured for the before/after table only. Mounts: a definition without a rear plate gets the vanilla plate mesh, by depot path, when a sibling definition of the same .app has a rear plate on the same slot: the sibling's placement is cast onto this definition's rear bumper mesh along the plate normal, and the plate goes mountGapMetres in front of the rearmost hit.
